Conclusion In this Listening component, candidates are assessed on their ability to understand and respond to information presented in a variety of forms; recognise, understand and distinguish between facts, ideas and opinions and select and organise material relevant to specific purposes. Therefore, candidates should listen to the recording very carefully and develop techniques to enable them to identify and select appropriate detail for their answers. They should gain as much practice as possible at listening exercises in class, and attempt past listening papers under timed conditions. Further work on expanding knowledge of Hindi vocabulary would also help. HINDI AS A SECOND LANGUAGE
notes.key_messages: • Candidates need to be encouraged to write their responses legibly to ensure meaning is clearly conveyed. • Candidates also need to ensure they read the questions carefully and take care to include all required details in their answers.
notes.general_comments: The majority of candidates appeared to be reasonably well prepared for this examination and tried to respond appropriately to the recording and questions. This paper is assessing “listening for understanding” and therefore reasonable spelling mistakes are accepted as long as they do not interfere with the communication of the correct answer. The majority of candidates made an attempt to answer each question.
